sourcePins.question: Which exact OpenAI mathematical claims overlap with executed Yang–Mills, energy and acoustic work, and which methods can be transferred with their assumptions intact?
acceptance: Screen complete catalogue metadata; disclose selected statement-level reading
Bind every overlap to exact target, hypotheses, data, limit and evidence path
Freeze independent skepticism before peer reports
Execute bounded tests and discriminating controls; preserve failures
Publish reviewed crosswalk, graph, roadmap and source-reading limits
notClaimed: Yang–Mills continuum solution from a finite model
Lean execution unless run and logged

claims.title: Continuum O(3) and our fixed-spacing gauge model
claims.external: Canonical continuum limit of 2D nearest-neighbor O(3) spins at beta→infinity, with field normalization, Schwinger convergence, OS reconstruction, positive gap and non-Gaussianity; formalization scope only finite-domain O(n) correlation decay.
claims.ours: Fixed-spacing Z^3 SU(2) patterned model: named-box whole-sequence state limit and inherited representation gap alpha/16. Uniform route-B fixed-a strong-coupling certificate has an explicit weak-coupling admission obstruction.
claims.missing: Different dimension, fields and action: S² spins vs SU(2) gauge links; No cutoff-uniform estimates or admissible g(a)→0 trajectory for present certificate; Same-field continuum normalization, reconstruction and nontriviality must be supplied; Finite-domain formalization cannot be promoted to continuum proof
claims.use: Use canonical length/field normalization and the separate field/gap/reconstruction obligations as a review template; no constants or theorem conclusions imported.
claims.proofScope: Selected publisher statement; no full proof audit or Lean execution. Family 215 formalization covers finite-domain correlations only.
claims.readingDepth: Introduction and main theorem clauses read; full proof not audited

claims.title: An entropy area law assumes a gap
claims.external: Entanglement entropy area law for finite induced Z² graph with fixed finite local dimension q, bounded finite-range interactions, unique ground vector and assumed uniform global spectral gap.
claims.ours: Reduced-state trace-norm locality and Wilson-loop area parity in fixed-spacing SU(2) model.
claims.missing: 2D finite-q bounded terms differ from Z³ infinite-dimensional SU(2) link Hilbert spaces and unbounded electric terms; Global spectral gap is a premise, not an output; Entanglement entropy area law is not Wilson-loop confinement area law; Any truncation requires q-dependent constants and cutoff removal
claims.use: Consider conditional-information or tensor approximations only in a separately specified finite-q planar truncation; existence does not provide efficient tensor construction.
claims.proofScope: Selected publisher statement; no full proof audit or Lean execution.
claims.readingDepth: Introduction and main theorem clauses read; full proof not audited

claims.title: A threshold state is not a mass gap
claims.external: For undeformed supersymmetric SU(N) BFSS on gauge-invariant L²(R^(9(N²−1)))⊗fermions, every fixed N≥2 has a one-dimensional zero kernel at the threshold of continuous spectrum.
claims.ours: SU(2) lattice gauge-invariant spectral analysis and representation-specific vacuum simplicity.
claims.missing: 0+1D supersymmetric matrix quantum mechanics differs from pure 3+1D Yang–Mills; Threshold zero eigenstate coexists with continuum starting at zero; it does not yield a positive spectral gap; Finite-N constants are not uniform in rank or continuum cutoff
claims.use: Retain full operator domain and norm-exhaustion checks when using deformations; no direct theorem transfer.
claims.proofScope: Selected publisher statement; no full proof audit or Lean execution.
claims.readingDepth: Introduction and main theorem clauses read; full proof not audited

claims.title: Our open continuum Yang–Mills goal
claims.external: Not located as an OpenAI catalogue problem; Clay 4D continuum Yang–Mills existence and mass gap.
claims.ours: Explicit open parent goal; accepted finite and fixed-spacing subproblems.
claims.missing: Nontrivial continuum QFT on R4 with required axioms; Physical mass scale and gap on same continuum fields; Uniform control along a valid continuum trajectory
claims.use: Keep open-continuum node open and add proposed-transfer edges from 215 rather than solved-equivalence edges.
claims.proofScope: No proof execution here; the project parent remains open.

claims.title: Generalized amplitude-damping classical capacity
claims.external: Single-letter unrestricted classical capacity and repeated-use Holevo additivity for every generalized amplitude-damping channel; paper additionally claims additivity with any finite-dimensional partner channel.
claims.ours: Single-qubit ergotropy, passive energy and energy closure after zero-temperature amplitude damping followed by dephasing; finite numerical validation.
claims.missing: No Holevo information objective, input ensemble optimization, decoder, or n-use entangled channel analysis exists in our code.; Our ergotropy is a different functional of a prepared state. Extra dephasing is a composition outside the exact displayed channel unless separately treated.
claims.use: Add generalized thermal damping and signed reservoir heat to our fixed-Hamiltonian qubit model, independently of capacity claims.
claims.proofScope: Publisher scope doc lists repeated-use capacity/additivity and scalar attained maximum; expressly excludes additivity with arbitrary different partner and separate-measurement decoding. No Lean proof was run here.
claims.readingDepth: Lines 1–295: model, main capacity theorem, arbitrary-partner additivity corollary, and beginning of proof strategy; not full proof audit.

claims.title: Entropy photon-number inequality
claims.external: For n modes of each independent input into a passive beam splitter, entropy photon number of output C is at least eta*N(rho_A)+(1-eta)*N(rho_B), where N(rho)=g^{-1}(S(rho)/n).
claims.ours: Two-dimensional qubit energy and ergotropy; no bosonic Fock-space beam splitter or entropy-power theorem.
claims.missing: No bosonic channel or receiver encoding is specified by the project.; A physical mode identification, measured input noise, cross-port independence and numerical cutoff/tail error would all need justification.
claims.use: Possible future thermal-noise bounds for an explicitly modeled bosonic receiver; entropy photon number is not output energy created without an input.
claims.proofScope: Publisher scope document selects the EPnI itself; thermal-attenuator and broadcast-capacity consequences are outside that selected formalization. No Lean proof was run here.
claims.readingDepth: First 160 lines: exact main theorem, equality model, thermal-attenuator corollary and surrounding assumptions; not full proof audit.

claims.title: Global classical relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell solutions
claims.external: Global unique classical solutions for the 3D one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system with arbitrary-size smooth compatible initial data in the stated class.
claims.ours: Driven fixed-mutual-inductance RLC circuits coupled to one mechanical mode; finite linear ODE/phasor energy identity.
claims.missing: Our lumped finite-dimensional reciprocal circuit is not this kinetic PDE and has no phase-space distribution or Maxwell initial-value problem.; A solution-existence result neither supplies an uncounted source nor predicts a circuit conversion efficiency.
claims.use: Keep as a distinct mathematical-physics node; do not attach a solved-by-us or energy-gain edge. Low priority for current tabletop protocol.
claims.proofScope: Scope document describes this selected global-existence theorem; proof not executed or independently audited in this lane.
claims.readingDepth: First 160 lines: equation, initial data, global classical-solution theorem and beginning of proof strategy; not full proof audit.

claims.title: Two-dimensional ground-state area law
claims.external: Entanglement entropy is bounded by C times boundary size for unique uniformly gapped ground states of bounded finite-range square-lattice Hamiltonians.
claims.ours: Single prepared qubit with fixed Hamiltonian, not an interacting two-dimensional ground-state family.
claims.missing: No such many-body Hamiltonian, unique ground state or uniform gap has been established in our qubit energy work.; A spectral gap is an input hypothesis, so this theorem cannot establish the missing Yang–Mills gap.; The associated PEPS existence statement is not by itself an efficient numerical construction.
claims.use: Conditional future tensor-network modeling after an independently justified many-body Hamiltonian and gap; no present theorem overlap.
claims.proofScope: Not assessed in this lane; no family-wide verified badge is inferred.
claims.readingDepth: First 160 lines: local-Hamiltonian class, exact gap hypothesis, area-law theorem and PEPS corollary; not full proof audit.

claims.title: Full boundary data versus finite resonances
claims.external: Full static boundary displacement-to-traction data identify both smooth real Lamé moduli on a bounded connected smooth three-dimensional domain with positive elastic energy.
claims.ours: Finite homogeneous-sphere forward modes, a passive fixture model, and finite transfer functions; existing source register explicitly distinguishes finite peaks from full boundary data.
claims.missing: Complete static displacement-to-traction operator; Matching smooth domain and coefficient assumptions; Reconstruction and stability beyond uniqueness; Calibrated experimental data and model discrepancy control
claims.use: Use calibrated force or traction and an explicit observability test before trying material inversion.
claims.proofScope: No full proof audit or Lean execution. Catalogue-only comparisons do not establish theorem truth.
claims.readingDepth: Manuscript pp.1–3 and full short scope page; no full proof audit or Lean execution

claims.title: Geometry recovery and companion scope
claims.external: Full zero-frequency patch boundary forms identify a smooth metric and a rank-two unitary connection up to patch-fixed diffeomorphism and unitary gauge.
claims.ours: Source comparison and measurement-coordinate caveats only; no metric/connection recovery theorem or solver.
claims.missing: Same extended boundary operator; Smooth manifold, rank-two Hermitian bundle and unitary connection model; Explicit gauge and coordinate quotient; Correct manuscript-specific verification
claims.use: Record measurement coordinates and gauge freedom; bind proof status to the exact companion statement.
claims.proofScope: lean/docs/365.md covers a different bounded measurable scalar-conductivity nonuniqueness companion; this distinction was already recorded by the project.
claims.readingDepth: Headline manuscript pp.1–3 and full scope page; no full proof audit or Lean execution

claims.title: Exact fast DFT versus our sampled FFT
claims.external: Deterministic exact-complex-arithmetic length-n DFT in O(n(log n)^(1-delta)) with explicit delta=10^-13 and a stated arithmetic model.
claims.ours: Ordinary floating-point radix-two FFT and finite synthetic acquisition checks, with no sub-n-log-n complexity construction.
claims.missing: Matching exact arithmetic and coefficient-cost model; New asymptotic algorithm and complete complexity proof
claims.use: Keep arithmetic complexity and floating-point acquisition as separate questions; no algorithm transfer claimed.
claims.proofScope: No full proof audit or Lean execution. Catalogue-only comparisons do not establish theorem truth.
claims.readingDepth: Catalogue only; manuscript proof not read

claims.title: Infinite convergence versus finite data
claims.external: Full-sequence almost-everywhere convergence of ordinary symmetric Fourier partial sums for every complex-valued function in L log L(T).
claims.ours: Finite sampled Fourier and signal identities, not an infinite-dimensional convergence proof.
claims.missing: Quantification over the full function class; Almost-everywhere full-sequence proof rather than a finite signal test
claims.use: Retain finite-band acquisition limitations; an infinite convergence statement does not recover unmeasured data.
claims.proofScope: No full proof audit or Lean execution. Catalogue-only comparisons do not establish theorem truth.
claims.readingDepth: Catalogue only; manuscript proof not read

experiments.title: A fixed-spacing certificate needs a new continuum bridge
experiments.result: Exact arithmetic confirms the current sufficient strong-coupling certificate cannot follow a trajectory g(a) → 0 indefinitely. Common ground-state projectors can coexist with gaps tending to zero.
experiments.limit: This is a limit of this certificate, not a disproof of a physical Yang–Mills mass gap.

experiments.title: Thermal damping has an explicit energy source
experiments.equation: p′ = (1 − γ)p + γν ; Q = hf γ(ν − p)
experiments.result: The generalized channel matches Kraus matrices and an energy-conserving reservoir dilation. 864 cases recover the existing zero-temperature calculator; separate reviewers checked six and three frozen states.
experiments.limit: State ergotropy is not channel capacity or apparatus efficiency. Inverted reservoirs are resources; no laboratory data.

experiments.title: Equal frequencies can hide unequal material parameters
experiments.equation: (E, ρ) → (aE, aρ) leaves f unchanged; static traction → a × traction
experiments.result: Independent roots and actual production calls confirm the common-scaling ambiguity. Calibrated mass or nonzero traction removes this direction in the two-parameter model. Unknown gain can hide a response-amplitude change.
experiments.limit: Hypothetical candidate materials, not copper changing density when moved. No general inverse-uniqueness or full-spectrum result.

experiments.title: Certify a finite energy identity algebraically
experiments.equation: H = kq²/2 + p²/(2m) ; Ḣ = u(p/m) − b(p/m)²
experiments.result: Exact coefficient cancellation and rational matrix checks agree. Wrong port definitions, negative damping, incorrect Gram factors and a misleading positive sampling grid are rejected.
experiments.limit: Requires m,k > 0 and b ≥ 0. This known identity is not a new theorem, a Lean build, a complete SOS system reproduction or a hardware test.

rounds.title: Compare the statements before transferring a result
rounds.summary: Six specialists inspected pinned project artifacts, the complete catalogue metadata and selected primary statements. The advisor froze all six reports before choosing the next tests.
rounds.criticism: Family IDs are not solved counts; related Hamiltonians are not identical problems; full boundary maps are not finite peaks; a proof may cover only a companion statement.
rounds.decision: Select four bounded physics/maths tests plus independent catalogue and skeptic gates. Freeze expected cases before producer inspection.
rounds.result: 32 candidate families screened; 10 distinct selected families retained in 12 comparisons including one separate open parent goal. No exact solved or exact attempted catalogue target established.

rounds.title: Execute the tests and preserve what failed
rounds.summary: The panel carried out the selected calculations and reviewed the results. The source parser’s CAT(0) link failure and an incorrect human-review label were corrected with receipts; frozen Round 1 remains intact.
rounds.criticism: A model passing its own tests is insufficient. Positive controls, wrong controls, statement scope and independent expected cases are needed.
rounds.decision: Accept only scoped model and workflow transfers; keep continuum existence, source-free power and full-object reconstruction open.
rounds.result: 93 exact gauge checks; 5,184 thermal cases; eight acoustic gates; 26 exact energy checks; 17 corpus controls; independent skeptic and three-state methods comparisons. No third research round.

roadmap.title: Pin each theorem before importing it
roadmap.action: Attach exact manuscript revision, target declaration, assumptions and conclusion to every proposed theorem edge. Preserve companion and headline distinctions.
roadmap.acceptance: Matching statements are reviewed and any claimed proof execution has a reproducible log and dependency/axiom record.
roadmap.status: Documentary gate implemented; Lean execution remains unperformed.

roadmap.title: Build a new continuum bridge for Yang–Mills
roadmap.action: Use family 215 as a list of obligations: scale/field normalization, same-field limits, reconstruction, nontriviality and a cutoff-uniform gap. Keep the existing strong-coupling gate visible.
roadmap.acceptance: A justified trajectory and estimates survive cutoff removal in the actual gauge model.
roadmap.status: Open research goal. Fixed-spacing results retained; no new continuum theorem.

roadmap.title: Make reservoir cost explicit in quantum experiments
roadmap.action: Use the tested thermal-channel module for parameter studies, then specify preparation, bath reset, switching and readout work before any apparatus claim.
roadmap.acceptance: All energy inputs and stored-energy changes are calibrated; a complete cycle closes within a predeclared uncertainty budget.
roadmap.status: Generalized channel code executed; apparatus measurements not performed.

roadmap.title: Add a calibrated acoustic observable
roadmap.action: For the copper experiment, combine repeatable finite-band frequency data with known mass or calibrated displacement/force and temperature/support controls. Randomize A/B/A positions and retain sensor-gain uncertainty.
roadmap.acceptance: The chosen parameterization is locally identifiable after nuisance parameters and model discrepancy are included.
roadmap.status: Scaling ambiguity and two-parameter discriminator tested; physical protocol remains proposed.

roadmap.title: Use exact certificates where the model permits them
roadmap.action: Extend exact energy identities only after defining domains, units and input/output ports; retain negative controls and separately check omitted physics.
roadmap.acceptance: Exact residual vanishes and the sign certificate holds on the declared domain; hardware claims receive independent measurements.
roadmap.status: Known one-mode identity verified exactly. No full SOS/Lean pipeline reproduced.
